key_insight: HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating provided the best oxidation protection for SA516 boiler steel, cutting maximum weight gain by 95.71% versus uncoated steel after 50 cycles at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: The result shows that dense NiCr-based ceramic composite coatings can substantially improve high-temperature durability of boiler steels in cyclic oxidizing environments.
method: Compared Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings deposited by HVOF and plasma spray.
Characterized phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports severe spalling and Fe2O3 formation on bare steel, while the HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating showed the largest reduction in mass gain and formed protective Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO scales.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated under laboratory cyclic oxidation only, so long-term service behavior under real boiler conditions, thermal shock, and erosion still needs validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
